title: Body sensations (physical reactions)
description: Physical sensations a client notices, used in the physical reactions slot of the five-part model and in panic, health anxiety, insomnia, eating and anger formulations; rated for intensity (0 to 100). Code the sensation here; a catastrophic reading of it is a thought, and what the client does about it is a behavior.
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 2 Understanding Your Problems
APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Racing or pounding heart
concepts.definition: Awareness of a fast, forceful or irregular heartbeat; a panic attack symptom often misread as a heart attack.
concepts.client_wording: My heart racing, pounding or skipping a beat.
concepts.example: Heart pounding while waiting to give a toast: "Something's wrong with my heart."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Shortness of breath
concepts.definition: Sensation of not getting enough air or of smothering, often with fast, shallow breathing.
concepts.client_wording: Like I can't get enough air in.
concepts.example: On a crowded train: "I'm going to suffocate."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Choking sensation or lump in throat
concepts.definition: Feeling of throat constriction or a lump that makes swallowing or speaking feel hard; occurs in fear and in sadness.
concepts.client_wording: A tight throat or lump that makes it hard to swallow.
concepts.example: Lump in my throat when I tried to speak at the funeral.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Chest tightness or pain
concepts.definition: Tightness, pressure or pain in the chest during arousal; new or unexplained chest pain needs medical assessment first.
concepts.client_wording: My chest feels tight, heavy or painful.
concepts.example: Band of pressure across my chest during an argument.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Dizziness or lightheadedness
concepts.definition: Feeling unsteady, lightheaded or about to faint; in panic often misread as a sign of imminent collapse.
concepts.client_wording: Lightheaded or wobbly, like I might pass out.
concepts.example: Dizzy in the shopping mall: "I'm going to collapse."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Weak or jelly legs
concepts.definition: Sensation of weakness or wobbliness in the legs, often feared as a sign of fainting or collapse.
concepts.client_wording: My legs feel weak, like they might give way.
concepts.example: Legs like jelly walking up to the podium.
sources: Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Trembling or shaking
concepts.definition: Visible or felt shaking of hands, legs, body or voice during anxiety or strong emotion.
concepts.client_wording: Shaky hands, legs or voice.
concepts.example: Hands shaking while signing my name in front of the clerk.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Sweating
concepts.definition: Increased sweating, especially palms, face or underarms, during anxiety; often monitored and hidden in social anxiety.
concepts.client_wording: Sweaty hands or face when I'm stressed.
concepts.example: Sweaty palms before shaking hands at the interview.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Hot flushes or chills
concepts.definition: Sudden waves of heat or cold through the body during anxiety or panic.
concepts.client_wording: Suddenly going hot or cold all over.
concepts.example: A wave of heat then chills in the doctor's waiting room.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Tingling or numbness
concepts.definition: Pins and needles or numbness, often in hands, feet or around the mouth, especially with fast breathing.
concepts.client_wording: Pins and needles or numb patches, often in hands or face.
concepts.example: Tingling fingers during a panic attack: "I'm having a stroke."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Clark-1986 § The cognitive model of panic

concepts.label: Dry mouth
concepts.definition: Dry, sticky mouth from reduced saliva during anxious arousal; can make speaking feel harder.
concepts.client_wording: My mouth goes dry when I'm nervous.
concepts.example: Mouth so dry I kept sipping water during my presentation.
sources: Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Blushing
concepts.definition: Visible reddening of face or neck in social situations; a feared, closely monitored symptom in social anxiety.
concepts.client_wording: My face going red in front of people.
concepts.example: Blushing when asked a question in class: "Everyone can see I'm anxious."
sources: Clark-Wells-1995 § The cognitive model of social phobia

concepts.label: Jumpy or easily startled
concepts.definition: Exaggerated startle to sudden noises or movement; a hyperarousal sign after trauma and in anxiety.
concepts.client_wording: Jumping out of my skin at sudden noises.
concepts.example: Leaping up when a door slammed down the hall.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (arousal and reactivity)
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Muscle tension
concepts.definition: Sustained tightening of muscles, often in the neck, shoulders, jaw or back; a core feature of generalized anxiety.
concepts.client_wording: Tight, tense muscles, often in my neck or shoulders.
concepts.example: Shoulders up by my ears by the end of the workday.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition

concepts.label: Aches and pains
concepts.definition: Headaches, muscle aches or soreness accompanying chronic tension, low mood or poor sleep; medical causes should be ruled out.
concepts.client_wording: Headaches or aching, sore muscles.
concepts.example: Tension headache every afternoon during exam week.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Generalized Anxiety Disorder (associated features)

concepts.label: Restlessness
concepts.definition: Physical restlessness or feeling keyed up and unable to settle; a criterion symptom of generalized anxiety disorder.
concepts.client_wording: Fidgety and keyed up, unable to sit still.
concepts.example: Pacing the kitchen waiting for test results.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Butterflies or churning stomach
concepts.definition: Fluttering, churning or knotted feeling in the stomach during nervous anticipation.
concepts.client_wording: Butterflies or a knot in my stomach.
concepts.example: Stomach churning on the drive to my first day at a new job.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Nausea
concepts.definition: Queasy, sick feeling, sometimes with gagging or retching; occurs in anxiety, panic and disgust.
concepts.client_wording: Feeling sick to my stomach, like I might throw up.
concepts.example: Queasy before every flight: "I'll be sick in front of everyone."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Panic Attack Specifier
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Sudden need for the toilet
concepts.definition: Sudden urge to empty bowel or bladder under stress, which can lead to avoiding places far from toilets.
concepts.client_wording: Suddenly needing the bathroom urgently when I'm stressed.
concepts.example: Needing the toilet three times before leaving for the bus.
sources: Clark-Beck-2010 § Ch. 1 Anxiety: A Common but Multifaceted Condition
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Stomach pain or sinking feeling
concepts.definition: Ache, cramp or sinking sensation in the gut during stress, dread, shame or envy.
concepts.client_wording: An ache or sinking feeling in my stomach.
concepts.example: Sinking feeling in my gut when the boss's email arrived.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Fatigue
concepts.definition: Persistent physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy not relieved by rest; distinct from sleepiness.
concepts.client_wording: Drained and out of energy, even after resting.
concepts.example: Too tired to shower after a full night in bed.
sources: Chalder-etal-1993 § Introduction
Shen-etal-2006 § Definitions of sleepiness and fatigue
APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder

concepts.label: Heavy limbs
concepts.definition: Heavy, leaden feeling in the arms or legs; termed leaden paralysis in depression with atypical features.
concepts.client_wording: My arms and legs feel as heavy as lead.
concepts.example: Legs too heavy to get off the sofa all afternoon.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Depressive Disorders, with atypical features specifier

concepts.label: Slowed down
concepts.definition: Felt slowing of movement, speech or thinking; termed psychomotor retardation when observable by others.
concepts.client_wording: Everything feels slow, like I'm moving in slow motion.
concepts.example: Took an hour to get dressed this morning.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Wired at bedtime
concepts.definition: Physical and mental arousal at bedtime that blocks sleep onset despite tiredness; central to cognitive models of insomnia.
concepts.client_wording: Tired but wired in bed, my body and mind won't switch off.
concepts.example: Lying awake at 1 a.m., heart thumping: "I'll be useless tomorrow."
sources: Harvey-2002 § A cognitive model of insomnia

concepts.label: Daytime sleepiness
concepts.definition: Tendency to doze or fall asleep during the day; differs from fatigue and can signal sleep loss or a sleep disorder.
concepts.client_wording: Struggling to keep my eyes open in the day.
concepts.example: Nodding off in afternoon meetings.
sources: Shen-etal-2006 § Definitions of sleepiness and fatigue

concepts.label: Waking unrefreshed
concepts.definition: Waking feeling unrested or unrecovered despite adequate time asleep.
concepts.client_wording: Waking up feeling like I haven't slept.
concepts.example: Eight hours in bed and I still woke up exhausted.
sources: Wilkinson-Shapiro-2012 § Definition of nonrestorative sleep

concepts.label: Waking in panic
concepts.definition: Waking abruptly from sleep in a surge of panic sensations, not caused by a nightmare; common in panic disorder.
concepts.client_wording: Jolting awake at night with my heart racing and full of fear.
concepts.example: Woke at 3 a.m. gasping with my heart pounding, no dream I could remember.
sources: Craske-Tsao-2005 § Characterization of nocturnal panic

concepts.label: Derealization
concepts.definition: Surroundings feel unreal, distant, dreamlike or visually distorted, while the person knows this is not literally so.
concepts.client_wording: The world looks unreal or far away, like a dream or a film.
concepts.example: In the busy store everything looked flat and fake: "I'm going crazy."
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder
Hunter-etal-2003 § Phenomenology
Holmes-etal-2005 § Detachment

concepts.label: Depersonalization
concepts.definition: Feeling detached from one's own body, thoughts, feelings or actions, as if an outside observer, while knowing this is not literally so.
concepts.client_wording: Disconnected from myself, like I'm watching from outside my body.
concepts.example: Talking at work but feeling like a robot watching myself speak.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder
Hunter-etal-2003 § Phenomenology
Holmes-etal-2005 § Detachment

concepts.label: Blanking out
concepts.definition: Blank, absent state in which attention drifts away from the present and time passes unnoticed; may be dissociative under stress.
concepts.client_wording: Spacing out or going blank, and missing what's happening.
concepts.example: During the argument I went blank and missed the last ten minutes.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Dissociative Disorders introduction
Holmes-etal-2005 § Detachment

concepts.label: Frozen (freeze response)
concepts.definition: Sudden inability to move or speak under extreme threat or trauma reminders; an automatic defensive response, not a choice.
concepts.client_wording: Frozen, unable to move or speak, even though I wanted to.
concepts.example: When he shouted I froze and couldn't say a word.
sources: Schauer-Elbert-2010 § Defense cascade
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Heat rising (anger)
concepts.definition: Heat surging into the face, neck or chest as anger builds; an early warning cue in anger management.
concepts.client_wording: Heat building in my face and chest when I'm getting angry.
concepts.example: Face burning as the driver cut in front of me.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Deffenbacher-2011 § Conceptualization of anger

concepts.label: Clenched jaw or fists
concepts.definition: Tightening of the jaw, hands or arms as the body readies to confront; a useful early anger cue.
concepts.client_wording: Gritting my teeth or balling my fists.
concepts.example: Fists clenched under the table while my father criticized me.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Pressure to explode
concepts.definition: Mounting internal pressure and energy with urges to hit, shout or lash out; signals rising risk of aggression.
concepts.client_wording: Like I'm about to explode or lose it.
concepts.example: Felt like I'd burst if he said one more word, so I walked out.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
Deffenbacher-2011 § Conceptualization of anger

concepts.label: Intense hunger
concepts.definition: Strong physical hunger, often after long gaps or dietary restriction, which raises vulnerability to binge eating.
concepts.client_wording: So hungry I can't think about anything else.
concepts.example: Skipped breakfast and lunch, ravenous by 4 p.m., then binged.
sources: Fairburn-2008 § Ch. 9 Dietary Restraint, Dietary Rules and Controlling Eating

concepts.label: Fullness or bloating
concepts.definition: Uncomfortable stomach fullness or bloating after eating; common when undereating is reversed and often misread as weight gain.
concepts.client_wording: Uncomfortably full or bloated after eating.
concepts.example: Bloated after a normal lunch: "I've gained weight already."
sources: Fairburn-2008 § Ch. 11 Underweight and Undereating
Fairburn-2008 § Ch. 8 Shape Concern, Shape Checking, Feeling Fat and Mindsets

concepts.label: Feeling fat
concepts.definition: Experience of feeling fat that often relabels other emotions or body states such as fullness, bloating, sweating or tight clothes.
concepts.client_wording: Suddenly feeling fat or huge in my body.
concepts.example: Felt fat all evening after an argument, though nothing about my body had changed.
sources: Fairburn-2008 § Ch. 8 Shape Concern, Shape Checking, Feeling Fat and Mindsets

concepts.label: Loss of appetite
concepts.definition: Reduced desire to eat during low mood, anxiety or grief; marked weight change warrants assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Not hungry at all, I can't face food.
concepts.example: Barely ate for a week after the breakup.
sources: APA-DSM5TR-2022 § Major Depressive Disorder
Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions

concepts.label: Tearful
concepts.definition: Welling up or crying, often with a tight throat; frequent crying spells can accompany depression, grief or overwhelm.
concepts.client_wording: Close to tears or crying more than usual.
concepts.example: Welled up in the car after dropping my son at college.
sources: Linehan-2015 § Emotion Regulation Handout 6 Ways to Describe Emotions
